subject: General Knowledge
description: Covers Jnanpith, Saraswati Samman, Vyas Samman, Sahitya Akademi, Booker, and Moortidevi.

questions.stem: The Jnanpith Award, India's highest literary honor, is given for outstanding contribution to literature in which languages?

options.option_text: Any of the 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India, plus English
Only Hindi and Sanskrit
Any language spoken by at least one million people in India
Only classical languages of India

questions.explanation: JNANPITH AWARD: Instituted in 1961 by the Bharatiya Jnanpith trust. It is the highest literary award in India. It is presented to Indian citizens for outstanding contribution towards literature in ANY of the 22 languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, PLUS English (English was added in 2018 when Amitav Ghosh became the first English writer to win). The first recipient was G. Sankara Kurup in 1965 for Malayalam. PYQ FREQUENCY: Highly repeated in SSC, State PSCs, Bank exams.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which literary award was instituted by the K. K. Birla Foundation in 1991 and is given annually for outstanding prose or poetry literary works in any of the 22 Indian languages published in the last 10 years?

options.option_text: Saraswati Samman
Vyas Samman
Sahitya Akademi Award
Moortidevi Award

questions.explanation: SARASWATI SAMMAN: Instituted in 1991 by the K.K. Birla Foundation. It is awarded for an outstanding literary work written in any of the 22 Indian official languages (Eighth Schedule) during the last 10 years. It carries a cash prize of Rs 15 lakh. Harivansh Rai Bachchan was the first recipient (for his four-volume autobiography). VYAS SAMMAN is also by K.K. Birla Foundation but is ONLY for works in Hindi. SAHITYA AKADEMI is given by the Sahitya Akademi. PYQ FREQUENCY: SSC CGL, RRB NTPC.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Vyas Samman is an Indian literary award given exclusively for literary works written in which language?

options.option_text: Hindi
Sanskrit
Any Eighth Schedule Language
Awadhi or Braj Bhasha

questions.explanation: VYAS SAMMAN: Instituted in 1991 by the K.K. Birla Foundation. UNLIKE the Saraswati Samman (which is for any 8th Schedule language), the Vyas Samman is restricted to outstanding literary works written in HINDI authored by an Indian citizen and published in the past 10 years. First winner: Ram Vilas Sharma. PYQ FREQUENCY: State PSCs (especially Hindi belt), SSC CGL.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Who among the following was the FIRST woman to win the Jnanpith Award?

options.option_text: Ashapoorna Devi
Mahasweta Devi
Amrita Pritam
Mahadevi Varma

questions.explanation:
FIRST WOMAN JNANPITH WINNER: Ashapoorna Devi, a prominent Bengali novelist and poet. She won it in 1976 for her magnum opus novel "Prothom Protishruti" (The First Promise). 
- Amrita Pritam (Punjabi) won it later in 1981.
- Mahadevi Varma (Hindi) won in 1982.
- Mahasweta Devi (Bengali) won in 1996. PYQ FREQUENCY: SSC, Railway, State PSCs static GK.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Sahitya Akademi Award, unlike the Jnanpith Award, recognizes works in how many languages?

options.option_text: 24 languages (22 Eighth Schedule languages + English and Rajasthani)
22 Eighth Schedule languages only
All mother tongues recorded in the Indian Census
Only 6 Classical Languages of India

questions.explanation: SAHITYA AKADEMI AWARD: Established in 1954, given by the Sahitya Akademi (India's National Academy of Letters). It is awarded annually to writers of the most outstanding books of literary merit published in any of the 24 MAJOR INDIAN LANGUAGES. These 24 languages include the 22 languages enumerated in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, PLUS English and Rajasthani. It carries a plaque and a cash prize of Rs 1 Lakh. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims, SSC CGL.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which international literary award is given to the best original full-length novel written in the English language and published in the UK or Ireland?

options.option_text: The Booker Prize
The Pulitzer Prize
The International Booker Prize
The Nobel Prize in Literature

questions.explanation:
THE BOOKER PRIZE: The leading literary award in the English speaking world. Awarded annually to the best novel written in English and published in the United Kingdom or Ireland. Famous Indian/Indian-origin winners include Salman Rushdie, Arundhati Roy, Kiran Desai, and Aravind Adiga.
- THE INTERNATIONAL BOOKER PRIZE is different: it is given to a book TRANSLATED into English and published in the UK/Ireland (e.g., Geetanjali Shree won for Tomb of Sand). 
- THE PULITZER PRIZE is for American journalism and arts. PYQ FREQUENCY: SSC CGL, Bank PO.

questions.stem: The Moortidevi Award is presented annually for literary work which emphasizes Indian philosophy and cultural heritage. It is instituted by:

options.option_text: Bharatiya Jnanpith Trust
K. K. Birla Foundation
Sahitya Akademi
Ministry of Culture, Government of India

questions.explanation: MOORTIDEVI AWARD: An annual literary award in India presented by the Bharatiya Jnanpith Trust (the same trust that presents the Jnanpith Award). It is given for an outstanding work in any Indian language (or English) that highlights Indian philosophy and cultural heritage. Named after Moortidevi, the mother of the trust's founder, Sahu Shanti Prasad Jain. First awarded in 1983 to Kannada writer C.K. Nagaraja Rao. PYQ FREQUENCY: State PSCs, UGC NET.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The inaugural Jnanpith Award (1965) was conferred on G. Sankara Kurup for his contributions to which language's literature?

options.option_text: Tamil — a classical language with ancient Sangam literary tradition
Kannada — language of Kuvempu and the Navodaya literary movement
Malayalam — a classical language of Kerala with rich literary heritage
Telugu — classical language known for Prabandha literary tradition

questions.explanation: G. Sankara Kurup received the first Jnanpith Award in 1965 for his Malayalam poem collection 'Odakkuzhal' (The Flute). Tamil is a common distractor because it is the oldest classical language, but the first Jnanpith went to a Malayalam writer, not Tamil.

questions.stem: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913. Which work was the primary basis for this recognition?

options.option_text: Gora — a novel exploring Hindu identity and caste questions in Bengal
Chokher Bali — a psychological exploration of widowhood in Bengal
Gitanjali — a devotional poem collection he translated into English prose
Manasi — an early verse collection marking his emergence as a major poet

questions.explanation: Tagore was awarded the Nobel Prize primarily for 'Gitanjali (Song Offerings)', which he himself translated from Bengali into English prose-poetry. 'Gora' is a tempting distractor as it is his most celebrated novel, but it was not the cited work for the Nobel award.

questions.stem: The Sahitya Akademi's 'Yuva Puraskar' encourages emerging Indian writers. What is the maximum permissible age for a writer to be eligible?

options.option_text: Below 30 years at the time of book publication date
Below 35 years at the time of book publication date
Below 40 years at the time of award application submission
Below 45 years at the time of receiving the award

questions.explanation: The Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar requires the author to be below 35 years of age at the time of publication of the eligible work. '30 years' is a common wrong recall; the threshold is 35, mirroring several other national youth awards in India.

questions.stem: The International Booker Prize and the Booker Prize are two distinct literary awards. Which statement correctly differentiates them?

options.option_text: Booker recognizes debut novels; International Booker honors career achievement
Booker is for original English fiction; International Booker is for fiction translated into English
Booker is for British and Irish authors only; International Booker is for Commonwealth writers
Booker rewards literary fiction only; International Booker also covers genre fiction

questions.explanation: The Booker Prize is awarded for the best original novel written in English; the International Booker Prize is awarded for the best fiction translated into English. Option C is wrong because the Booker Prize was expanded in 2014 to include authors from any country writing in English, not just Commonwealth.

questions.stem: Which body administers the Jnanpith Award, India's highest literary recognition conferred since 1965?

options.option_text: Sahitya Akademi — an autonomous institution under Ministry of Culture
Bharatiya Jnanpith — a literary and cultural trust founded in 1944
National Book Trust — a Government of India body under Ministry of Education
Indian Council for Cultural Relations — under Ministry of External Affairs

questions.explanation: The Jnanpith Award is administered by Bharatiya Jnanpith, a private literary and cultural trust established in 1944 by Sahu Shanti Prasad Jain. The Sahitya Akademi Award is the most common distractor since many candidates conflate the two institutions, but Sahitya Akademi runs a separate award.

questions.stem: Among the following Jnanpith Award winners, who wrote in URDU and is often mistakenly grouped with Hindi literature due to shared geography and script similarity?

options.option_text: Sumitranandan Pant — celebrated Hindi Chayavad poet from Uttarakhand
Ramdhari Singh Dinkar — known for nationalist Veer Ras Hindi poetry
Firaq Gorakhpuri — Urdu poet whose real name was Raghupati Sahay
Mahadevi Varma — revered as the 'Meera of Modern Hindi' poetry

questions.explanation: Firaq Gorakhpuri (real name: Raghupati Sahay) won the Jnanpith Award in 1969 for his Urdu poetry collection 'Gul-e-Naghma'. Despite being from Gorakhpur — a Hindi-belt city — he wrote in Urdu. Pant (1968), Dinkar (1972), and Mahadevi Varma (1982) all won for Hindi, making Firaq the correct answer.

questions.stem: Amrita Pritam, the 1982 Jnanpith Award winner, wrote 'Ajj Aakhaan Waris Shah Nuu', addressing the 18th-century Punjabi poet Waris Shah. This poem was a lament triggered by which historical event?

options.option_text: The Bengal Famine of 1943 — a catastrophe that ravaged millions in Eastern India
The Partition of India in 1947 — which caused unprecedented communal violence in Punjab
The Emergency period of 1975–77 — which suppressed literary and creative freedom
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919 — a colonial atrocity in the heart of Punjab

questions.explanation: Amrita Pritam wrote 'Ajj Aakhaan Waris Shah Nuu' (Today I Invoke Waris Shah) as a cry of grief over the mass violence of the 1947 Partition, which devastated Punjab on both sides of the border. She invokes Waris Shah — author of the Punjabi epic Heer Ranjha — as a fellow witness to Punjab's suffering. Jallianwala Bagh is a tempting distractor due to its Punjabi setting, but that massacre predates Amrita Pritam's literary career.
